verdict.rationale: Missive documents an official MCP server that external AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can connect to and act on conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts "with the permissions you choose." That is a first-party permission-scoping capability for agent access, but the evidence never describes how the credentials are issued, which scopes exist, or whether REST API tokens can be restricted. The custom-scopes option for Missive's own outbound MCP client connections is a different capability and gets no credit here. missing for 10: documented scope/permission model for API tokens, per-agent credential issuance and revocation details, read-only or resource-level granularity, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
